quote: a continuous or broken line marked upon the surface of a highway by paint or otherwise to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions
reason: A centerline is a marking on a road surface, a feature of a place, not a set of road users.

quote: two or more vehicles coupled together

quote: That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks on opposite sides of the highway
reason: A crosswalk is a part of a highway, a place, not a set of road users.

quote: a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section
reason: A divided highway is a kind of place, not a set of road users.

quote: every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle
reason: A driver is a relational role held over a vehicle, so it is mapped as a role and never as class membership of the controlled vehicle.

quote: the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic
reason: A highway is a place, not a set of road users.

quote: The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines, or, if none, then the lateral boundary lines of the roadways of two highways which join one another
reason: An intersection is an area, a place, not a set of road users.

quote: every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.

quote: every sign, signal, marking and device not inconsistent with chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS or prohibited by law, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic
reason: A traffic-control device is roadside equipment placed by an authority, not a tracked road user.

quote: every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic or to make arrests for violations of traffic laws, ordinances or regulations

quote: the Department of Transportation or the local authority having jurisdiction to enact laws or ordinances or adopt regulations relating to traffic over a highway

quote: the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian
reason: A right-of-way is a relational right between road users in a scene, not a set of road users.

quote: that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder
reason: A roadway is a portion of a highway, a place, not a set of road users.

quote: the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city when any part of such highway is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic
reason: A street is a place, not a set of road users.

quote: every highway or portion thereof on which vehicular traffic is given the right-of-way
reason: A through highway is a place, not a set of road users.

quote: pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel
reason: The definition enumerates an extensional set of road users, the condition of using a highway for travel being context the using rule carries rather than membership.

quote: any official traffic-control device, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad, by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed
reason: A traffic-control signal is a device placed by an authority, not a tracked road user.

quote: every motor vehicle which is used for the transportation or delivery of goods with a body built and designed for that purpose
reason: The definition denotes an extensional set of road users, the goods-carrying motor vehicles bodied for that purpose, which the ontology's classes can classify.

quote: every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; (3) Electric personal assistive mobility devices as defined in NRS 482.029; and (4) An electric scooter.
reason: The definition denotes an extensional set of road users by an admitting clause and a closed list of exceptions, which the ontology's classes can classify.

quote: the territory contiguous to and including a highway when within any 600 feet along such highway there are buildings in use for business or industrial purposes

quote: an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions

quote: the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not
